title: Rationalized Difference Quotient of the Square Root
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: For f(x)=sqrt(x), simplify the difference quotient (f(x+h)-f(x))/h, h != 0, by rationalizing the numerator.

steps.title: Set Up the Quotient
steps.explanation: Substituting the rule into the difference quotient leaves a difference of roots on top.
steps.why: Direct cancellation of h is impossible because h appears only inside the roots.

steps.title: Multiply by the Conjugate
steps.explanation: Rationalize by multiplying numerator and denominator by the conjugate sqrt(x+h)+sqrt(x).
steps.why: Conjugate multiplication removes radicals from the numerator.

steps.title: Use the Difference of Squares
steps.explanation: The numerator becomes (x+h)-x = h, a clean linear expression.

steps.title: Cancel h
steps.explanation: Cancel the factor h between numerator and denominator (h != 0) to obtain the final form.
steps.why: The canceled h is exactly what made the quotient finite as h tends to 0.
